hero.title: Electrical Engineering Post Graduation in France
hero.subtitle: Studying Postgraduate (PG) Electrical Engineering in France is a great opportunity for students who want to gain advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in electrical power systems, renewable energy, automation, electronics, smart grids, and industrial control. The French universities and engineering schools offer specialized master's programs combining theory, lab work, research projects and industry experience.

overview: Studying Postgraduate (PG) Electrical Engineering in France is a great opportunity for students who want to gain advanced technical knowledge and professional skills in electrical power systems, renewable energy, automation, electronics, smart grids, and industrial control. The French universities and engineering schools offer specialized master's programs combining theory, lab work, research projects and industry experience.
Students who are planning to pursue \\PG Electrical Engineering in France\\ have a lot of benefits to opt for France.

Eligibility to Pursue PG Electrical Engineering in France The eligibility criteria for Indian students who are willing to pursue \\PG Electrical Engineering in France\\ generally include: - Bachelor degree in \\Electrical Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronics, Energy Engineering\\ or equivalent. A solid basis in mathematics, electrical circuits, electrical machines, electronics, power systems or control engineering depending on the program. - Good academic performance in undergraduate studies. - English language proficiency for English-taught programs, where applicable. - Language skills in French for French-taught programs if applicable. - Other academic or technical requirements as specified by the institution. Students with degrees in \\Instrumentation Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Mechatronics and Energy Engineering\\ may also be eligible for certain programs provided their previous academic work is relevant to the course requirements.

sections.title: Why Study Electrical Engineering in France?
sections.lead: Students who are planning to pursue \\PG Electrical Engineering in France\\ have a lot of benefits to opt for France.

items: \\Recognised Qualifications:\\ Public universities confer nationally recognized master's degrees, engineering schools provide specialized programs with their own qualification and recognition arrangements.
\\Advanced Specialisations:\\ Students can explore \\electrical power engineering, renewable energy, power electronics, control systems and industrial automation.
\\Renewable Energy and Smart Grids:\\ The programs may cover electricity distribution, energy efficiency, smart grids and intelligent power networks.
\\Research Opportunities:\\ Lab projects, research internships, and industry placements may provide hands-on experience.
\\International Study Options:\\ There are several \\master's programs in Electrical Engineering in France\\ that are fully taught in English, others require knowledge of French.
\\Global Career Opportunities\\: Graduates can work in the fields of electrical design, power systems, automation, energy management, electronics and research and development.

sections.lead: A French national \\Master's degree in Electrical Engineering\\ usually lasts two years (Master 1 (M1) and Master 2 (M2)), i.e. a total of 120 ECTS credits. Some programs allow direct admission to M2 for candidates with relevant previous qualifications.

items: \\Popular Electrical Engineering postgraduate specializations in France\\ include:
Power Engineering (Electrical)

Electrical Machines and Conversion of Energy
Power Systems and High Voltage Engineering
Signal Processing and Instrumentation
Intelligent Systems and Mechatronic

Electric Vehicle Electrical Systems

These \\postgraduate Electrical Engineering courses in France\\ help students to acquire specialized knowledge in modern electrical technologies, energy systems, industrial applications and intelligent engineering solutions.

sections.title: Admission Procedure for PG in Electrical Engineering in France
sections.lead: Students who are interested in \\pursuing a Master's in Electrical Engineering in France\\ generally need to follow the below steps:

items: 1. \\Research Programmes:\\ Compare universities by discipline, degree type, language of instruction and tuition fees.
2. \\Check Eligibility:\\ Verify that your undergraduate degree and prior coursework meet the academic requirements.
3. \\Required Documents:\\Gather your transcripts, degree certificates, CV, motivation letter, and language certificates if needed.
4. \\Submit the Application:\\ Apply via the university's official portal or through the application route relevant to your nationality and program.
5. \\Complete any Assessment:\\ Please attend an interview or provide additional information as requested.
6. \\Get the Decision:\\ Think about the offer, fee terms, deadlines and entry requirements.
7. \\Plan your finances:\\ Have a budget for tuition fees, living expenses and other costs.
8. \\Complete Visa Formalities\\ If applicable, complete the relevant Campus France and French student-visa procedures.

sections.title: Accreditation & Recognition
sections.lead: Students must verify the exact qualification awarded before accepting an offer for a \\postgraduate Electrical Engineering program in France\.

items: A French \\diplôme national de master\\ is an officially recognized qualification in the French higher education system and in the European higher education area. It generally means five years of study beyond the secondary level when added to the previous bachelor-level study.
Check before you sign up:
The official title of the degree.
If the program leads to a national master degree or an engineering diploma.
The status of recognition or accreditation of the institution.
The academic credits and length.
Recognition requirements for further education or employment in your destination country.
Students who are planning to return to India should consult prospective employers, universities or relevant authorities to determine qualification and employment requirements.

Salary in Electrical Engineering in France

There is no average salary for all \\Electrical Engineering graduates in France\. Salary will vary depending on the position, the location, the company, your prior experience, your language skills and whether it is an internship or a permanent job.

Applicants are to compare current job advertisements and salary surveys for their preferred specialization. When looking over an offer they should also consider taxes and social contributions, accommodation and other living expenses.

faqs.q: How long is a postgraduate electrical engineering course in France?
faqs.a: In France, a national \\Master's degree in Electrical Engineering\\ usually corresponds to a two-year course (M1 and M2) for a total of 120 ECTS credits. Some programs and engineering qualifications have different structures.

faqs.q: Can Indian students do Electrical Engineering PG in France?
faqs.a: Yes \\Indian students can study postgraduate Electrical Engineering in France\\ if they meet the academic, language and documentation criteria. University admission and student-visa approval are two different processes.

faqs.q: Is IELTS required for electrical engineering in masters in France?
faqs.a: Not always. \\French master's programs taught in English\\ may accept IELTS, TOEFL, another approved language test or evidence of previous English-medium education where permitted. Some taught programs in French may require you to have knowledge of French.

faqs.q: What is the tuition fee for PG in Electrical Engineering in France?
faqs.a: For 2026-2027, the reference fee for a national master's degree in the covered public institutions is €255 per year for EU/EEA/Swiss students and €3,950 for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Special programs and exemptions may alter the amount payable.

faqs.q: What are the career prospects after PG in Electrical Engineering in France?
faqs.a: Graduates can find jobs in \\electrical design, power systems, renewable energy, power electronics, automation, smart grids, embedded systems, and research and development.\\ Opportunities depend on technical expertise, experience, language ability and employer requirements.

faqs.q: Is it possible to study Electrical Engineering in France in English?
faqs.a: Yes. \\Electrical Engineering master's programs in English\\ (including specialized programs in smart grids and energy systems) are offered in selected French universities and engineering institutions. Students should check the language of instruction and language requirements for each program.
